brief:
Eye on Palestine published an illustrated narrative titled "The Map That Lost Its Names," following a character named Maryam as she journeys across Palestine to restore its cities to maps through stories and memories. The work presents a beautifully illustrated account centered on recovering place names and their significance to Palestinian identity and history.

The story frames the restoration of Palestinian geography as both a personal and cultural act, linking named places to lived experience and historical recollection. By connecting Maryam's journey to collective memory, the narrative suggests that while official maps may be altered or redrawn, the memory of Palestinian cities and their names persists beyond cartographic erasure.

title: Illustrated story restores Palestinian city names to maps through memory
